name: Zadar
title: Zadar Ship Gauging: UTM at Gaženica for Ferries and Cargo
description: Ship thickness gauging in Zadar: ultrasonic readings on island ferries, ro-pax, cruise and cargo ships at Gaženica and the old harbour, for surveys and checks.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Ships Calling at Zadar
intro: Zadar is the gateway to the northern Dalmatian islands, with a busy ferry harbour in the old city and a modern cargo and passenger port at Gaženica, a few kilometres to the south-east. Island ferries, ro-pax ships to Italy, cruise vessels and general cargo ships all call. Atlantis NDT sends gauging technicians from India to Zadar, working alongside, at a lay-by berth or from a launch at anchor.

highlights.h: Two ports for two kinds of ship
highlights.p: The old harbour handles island ferries close to the city, while Gaženica takes larger ro-pax, cruise and cargo ships, so the access and the working windows differ depending on where the ship is berthed.

highlights.h: Ferries that run on tight rotas
highlights.p: Island services around Ugljan, Pašman, Dugi Otok and the outer islands keep ferries moving most of the day, and gauging is best planned around overnight stops or winter lay-up.

highlights.h: No large drydock on the spot
highlights.p: Zadar is a port for passenger and cargo calls rather than heavy repair, so docking surveys usually take place at a yard elsewhere on the Adriatic, with pre-docking gauging done here.

port.h: The port of Zadar: the old harbour, Gaženica and the island channels
p: Zadar occupies a narrow peninsula on the Dalmatian coast, facing a chain of long, thin islands that shelter the Zadar channel. The port is managed by the Zadar Port Authority and works from two main areas. The old harbour at the city is used by the local ferry lines and smaller craft, and its quays sit within sight of the old town walls. The newer Gaženica port, built south-east of the centre to take heavier traffic away from the historic waterfront, has deeper berths, space for vehicles and cargo, and a terminal for passengers. Most large ships now use Gaženica, while the old harbour keeps the short-hop island services.

The mix of traffic is distinctly Adriatic. National ferry company vessels run to Ugljan, Pašman, Dugi Otok, Iž, Molat and other islands; ro-pax ferries have connected Zadar with Ancona in Italy; cruise ships visit in season; and general cargo ships, timber carriers and the occasional bulk vessel use Gaženica's cargo quays. Inshore, marinas and charter fleets fill the waters, but these craft are small and sit outside the scope of ship gauging. Winter timetables are lighter, so ferry operators often use the quieter months for maintenance, and that is the period when thickness gauging on island vessels is easiest to arrange without disrupting service.

The channel between the mainland and the islands is sheltered but narrow in places, and the strong north-easterly bora and the southerly jugo both influence berthing and boat transfers. Anchorage is possible off the port for ships that arrive ahead of their berth time or are waiting for orders, and launches reach those ships through the agent. The tidal range is small, so ships alongside rise and fall very little during a shift. Because the port is built for movement rather than for lay-up, a ship staying for several days in Zadar is the exception, and any job that needs more than a call-day window should be planned with the operator in advance.

facilities.h: Where gauging can happen at Zadar
p: At Gaženica, the large passenger and cargo berths give the best access in Zadar. A ro-pax ship waiting between sailings, or a cargo ship alongside after discharge, can have decks, ramps, ballast tanks and holds measured while the crew and the ship's engineers prepare spaces for entry. The terminal operator and the ship's agent control access, and gauging has to fit around loading, bunkering and the ship's own safety routines. Where a ship stays overnight, a more thorough programme becomes realistic.

The old harbour is better suited to smaller ferries and lay-overs, where the vessel is idle for a few hours or longer in winter. Full docking survey work usually requires a yard, and Zadar is not set up as a repair port, so owners point their ferries to a yard further along the coast or across the Adriatic. In those cases, pre-docking gauging in Zadar gives the yard a realistic steel estimate before the ship sails, and a return visit after the yard period can confirm that renewed plating and repaired areas meet the agreed values.
list: Gaženica passenger berths — vehicle decks, ramps, stern doors and ballast tanks on ro-pax and large ferries between sailings
Gaženica cargo quays — holds, hatch covers and tank tops on general cargo and timber ships after discharge
Old harbour ferry quays — island ferries on overnight stops or winter lay-up, with decks, voids and ballast tanks gauged
Cruise berths at Gaženica — scrubber piping and technical spaces during a call day
Zadar roads anchorage — launch access for pre-purchase and pre-docking condition gauging on waiting ships
Pre- and post-yard visits — gauging before a ferry leaves for its docking and again once repaired areas are complete

context.h: Regulation, ferry safety and the Dalmatian trade
p: Foreign-flag ships in Zadar are subject to port state control under the Paris MoU, with inspections carried out by Croatian officers under the harbour master's authority for the Zadar area. Domestic ferries and ro-pax ships also fall under the EU rules for passenger ships on scheduled routes, with regular surveys of structure, watertight integrity and vehicle decks. Corrosion at ramp hinges, drain lines and ballast tank boundaries is a frequent finding on older ferries, so owners use gauging to see how much margin remains before the next survey.

The EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials for larger ships calling at EU ports, and ships above the size thresholds come under EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime. For island ferry fleets, many of them decades old, steel condition is the main factor in deciding whether to renew plating, refit, or replace. Zadar's economy depends on tourism and on trade with the islands, so cargo ships calling here tend to carry building materials, timber and general goods rather than heavy bulk. Local knowledge of the ferry rotas helps us plan, because a ferry that sits idle for three hours at midday is a different opportunity from one that leaves every ninety minutes.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Zadar
jobs.p: Zadar jobs mirror the port's traffic. Ferry operators want vehicle decks, ramps and ballast tanks gauged in winter or during overnight stops; cargo owners want hatch covers, coamings and holds checked after discharge; owners planning a docking elsewhere want a measured steel estimate in advance. We agree sequence and reporting with the superintendent so that the readings suit class formats and the yard's planning needs.
list: Winter gauging of an island car ferry at the old harbour: vehicle deck, ramp hinges, drain lines, voids and ballast tanks
Ro-pax stern door and vehicle deck readings at Gaženica between Ancona sailings, closing out items noted at the last annual survey
Pre-docking steel estimate on a ferry before she sails to a yard on the Adriatic, covering bottom-adjacent tanks accessible afloat
Hatch covers and tank tops on a general cargo ship after discharge at a Gaženica quay, in preparation for an intermediate survey
Follow-up gauging after yard repairs, confirming that renewed plates and local repairs meet the measured values the owner expects

logistics: Zadar Airport has seasonal European services, and Zagreb offers year-round connections with a motorway running down to the coast; Split is also reachable by road. The ship's agent or the ferry operator arranges terminal access at Gaženica and the old harbour, and books launches for ships at anchor. The team travels from India on Schengen visas, so the visa schedule sets the earliest start date. Because ferries run tight rotas, the exact working window should be confirmed with the operator as soon as it is fixed.

faqs.q: Can ferries be gauged between sailings in Zadar?
faqs.a: In many cases yes, if the stop is long enough. A midday or overnight lay-over gives time for vehicle decks, ramps and any ballast tank the crew has made safe. We agree the scope with the operator beforehand so that the highest-priority areas are gauged first and nothing is left half done when the ferry sails.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Zadar for ferries?
faqs.a: Zadar is a passenger and cargo port rather than a repair port, so docking surveys are normally done at a yard elsewhere on the Adriatic. We carry out the pre-docking gauging in Zadar, so the yard has a steel estimate before the ship arrives, and can return afterwards to check repaired areas.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Gaženica and the old harbour for gauging?
faqs.a: Gaženica has deeper berths and more room for staging, and larger ships stay longer there, so it suits fuller programmes. The old harbour suits smaller island ferries and winter lay-up. The agent confirms which berth the ship will use and what access the terminal allows.

faqs.q: Does wind affect work in Zadar?
faqs.a: It can. A strong bora can interrupt launch transfers and make staging on open decks unsafe, so we keep a spare day in the plan for ships at anchor. Work inside tanks and holds, or alongside in the lee of the quay, is less affected.
